RepositoryOrchestrator.addRepositoryToProject() uses resolveCredential() and injectCredentialToken() instead of the old injectCredentials() call.

When resolveCredential() returns null for an HTTPS repository, the operation fails with a descriptive error message: "Repository '<name>' requires a credential for host '<host>'. Please select a credential in the repository settings."

summary: Reviewed 6 source files spanning the full credential pipeline: git-credentials.ts (resolveCredential, injectCredentialToken, stripEmbeddedCredentials, extractHost), workspace-orchestrator.ts, repository-orchestrator.ts, config.ts (parseGitCredentials), config routes (credentials CRUD, credential-options), and git-clone.ts / git-cli.ts. No Critical or High severity findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 — Broken Access Control: No issues. Path-traversal guards using path.resolve() + startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep) are applied consistently in all clone and delete paths in both orchestrators. The STABLE workspace ID is correctly protected from deletion. No privilege escalation vectors identified in the credential pipeline.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures: Medium (informational) — Credential tokens (PATs/passwords) are stored in plaintext in config.json. This is consistent with the tool's current design as a local developer utility, not a multi-tenant server. However, if the config.json is world-readable or stored in a shared location, tokens could be exposed. Recommendation: document in the README that config.json must be chmod 600 or equivalent, and consider adding OS-level chmod enforcement in config loading (chmodSync import is already present in config.ts but its usage in this context was not observed). No encryption at rest is a design limitation, not a code defect. Severity: Low/Info — does not block approval.

A02 — Token masking: Token masking is correctly applied in all API responses. The GET /api/config/credentials and GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options endpoints mask tokens (last 4 chars only). Raw tokens are never serialised into HTTP responses. stripEmbeddedCredentials() is applied to git stderr output before logging to ErrorLogManager, preventing token leakage in error logs. Well-implemented.

A03 — Injection: No issues. git is spawned with shell: false (git-cli.ts line 50), eliminating shell injection. Arguments are passed as a typed string array — no string concatenation. Token injection into URLs uses WHATWG URL object property assignment (parsed.username = token) with automatic percent-encoding — not string concatenation. URL allowlist in git-clone.ts blocks dangerous transport protocols (ext::, rsh::). No SQL, template, LDAP, or OS command injection vectors identified.

A04 — Insecure Design: Medium (informational) — resolveCredential() has a documented host/credential coherence gap: when credentialId is supplied, only an exact id match is performed with no cross-validation that the credential's host matches the repository URL's hostname (git-credentials.ts lines 104-111). The JSDoc flags this as caller responsibility. Currently the orchestrators set credentialId only from repo.CredentialId (user-chosen from the credential-options endpoint which already filters by host), so the risk surface is narrow. A defence-in-depth check in the orchestrators (assert credential.host === extractHost(repo.Url)) would close this gap if the call pattern ever widens. Severity: Low — informational, no immediate exploitability.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration: No Critical/High issues. The server listens on localhost by default (localised risk). Error messages are descriptive but do not leak stack traces or internal paths to the client. The git process environment explicitly suppresses credential helpers (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_ASKPASS=echo), preventing the git process from hanging or leaking system keychain credentials. PUT /api/config/webserver-url correctly blocks javascript:, data:, and vbscript: schemes.

A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components: No new dependencies were introduced by this WP. Implementation and tests use only Node.js built-ins (node:fs, node:path, node:child_process) and the WHATWG URL API — no third-party packages with CVE exposure. No dependency risk.

A07 — Authentication Failures: The tool does not implement authentication between the GUI and the local HTTP server (by design — local-only tool). Credential storage is in config.json, access-controlled at the OS filesystem level. No session tokens, cookies, or rate-limiting concerns apply to this WP's changes.

A08 — Software & Data Integrity: No issues. The credential pipeline does not involve deserialization of untrusted binary data. parseGitCredentials() performs structural validation (non-empty id/label/host/token, duplicate id check) before accepting credential entries from config.json.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring: Credential-missing events are correctly logged via ErrorLogManager with Source: 'credentials' and Severity: 'error', including structured Context (ProjectId, WorkspaceId, RepositoryId). Clone failure stderr is scrubbed of embedded credentials before logging (stripEmbeddedCredentials). Audit trail for credential-missing is complete and does not expose sensitive values.

A10 — SSRF: The tool clones git repositories whose URLs come from the user-configured repository store (not from untrusted external input at request time). URL allowlist in git-clone.ts restricts schemes to https://, http://, git://, ssh://, git@, file://, and absolute paths. No server-side URL fetch is triggered by inbound HTTP requests. SSRF risk is limited to the tool operator's own configuration; no external-input → server-fetch path exists.

Cleartext transport warning: http:// and git:// are on the URL allowlist and trigger a console.warn (git-clone.ts line 61-65), but are not blocked. These protocols transmit credentials in cleartext. For a local developer tool this is an acceptable informational warning, but if the tool is ever used in a shared or CI environment, blocking http:// when credentials are being injected would be a stronger defence. Severity: Low — informational.
